company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem (Data Operating Layer: Transform + Catalog + Quality)

routing_rationale: Builder-CTO archetype, technical co-founder with architecture-layer ownership. Security architecture sits with him by default (no CISO; he listed 'security' as a spoke of the platform at Snowflake Summit 2025). Distinct angle from the other three Coalesce contacts: declared control intent vs. effective permission state — the narrow gap CSPM config-checks don't fully close, named honestly without strawmanning the tooling Satish already runs.

research_summary.trigger_event: SYNQ acquisition + Coalesce Quality launch (March 10, 2026, 51 days prior). Satish commented substantively using a 'tap water' trust metaphor anchored in his pre-Coalesce financial-services data work.
research_summary.key_insight: Satish thinks in trust-as-engineering-outcome. Quoting his SYNQ comment verbatim risks surveillance frame for a sparse poster — operate in his frame without using his words. He runs the SOC 2 program + has CSPM tooling — strawmans against existing tools fail. The honest narrow gap is intent-vs-effective-state, which CSPM config-checks don't fully reconcile.

draft.body:
Coalesce Quality closes the loop on data trust at the consumer's cadence — drift between declared and true is caught before the consumer notices.

The same shape applies one layer down: declared control intent and effective permission state drift apart in ways CSPM config-checks don't fully reconcile.

The reconciliation between the two is what Transilience operates on — continuous, with humans in the loop on remediation, additive to existing CSPM.

Are you solving this at the IaC layer or pulling it up to the platform?
draft.architecture: signal-to-question — Coalesce Quality framing as analog, then the narrow architectural asymmetry, then product mention, then a substantive engineering question

verdict_history.reason: 'still verified on the cadence of a SOC 2 audit cycle' — implied lag to a CTO who built the SOC 2 program.

Was shipped initially. User-level review caught: (a) duplicated four-item product line across three Coalesce drafts, (b) cadence-asymmetry strawman against a CISO running CSPM, (c) no preemption of category-incumbent (Wiz/Drata) reflex, (d) newsletter-shaped subject.

Cross-draft witness flagged the parenthetical definitions as condescending to an architecturally fluent CTO; also flagged 'Transilience runs' echo with Justin and 'Curious' CTA echo across all three Coalesce drafts.

Stripped parentheticals, inverted product sentence ('is what Transilience operates on'), reset subject to flat technical 'Permission state vs declared intent', dropped 'Curious' CTA prefix. All four cross-draft fingerprints resolved.

witness.what_works: Subject is flat technical, drops the newsletter-shaped 'after Quality' pattern. Opener anchors in Coalesce Quality's logic. The narrow asymmetry (intent vs effective state, CSPM doesn't reconcile) is the *real* gap, not a strawman. The product sentence is structurally distinct from the other two Coalesce drafts (substance-first inversion vs subject-first). CSPM-incumbent reflex preempted in one phrase ('additive to existing CSPM'). CTA is a substantive architectural question.
witness.what_fails: 'Additive to existing CSPM' is the only line a Coalesce reader could compare side-by-side with Justin's email and notice as a thematic match — though the surrounding language is fully distinct. The structural echo is now thematic only, not lexical.

review_flags: coordinate-across-coalesce-leads: do not send Satish, Mike, Justin, Cyrille in same week. Recommended: one per fortnight, bottom-up by seniority
